target_customer: Landlords of multifamily buildings who pay for guaranteed rent and fast leasing, and renters who lease through the app
problem: Landlords carry vacancy risk and slow leasing. Rezi guaranteed monthly rent and paid up to 12 months upfront while handling leasing remotely.
business_model: Rent guarantee and lease-up marketplace funded by debt, earning a spread on leases
product_category: Proptech rental marketplace with rent guarantee

founders.name: Sean Mitchell
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. Later launched a new startup, Ryse, per search coverage.

founders.name: Keenan D. Williams
founders.background_notes: YC page notes RevOps, GTM and sales enablement background.

founders.name: Harsh Yadav
education: National Institute of Technology Allahabad, B.Tech

exit.reason: Mitchell attributed it to scaling costs, lack of profitability and costlier financing as rates rose, per The Real Deal summary.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly marketplace and leasing software. The hard parts were financial and operational, namely underwriting rent guarantees at scale, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Rent guarantees depend on cheap capital rather than a technical moat, and any well-funded proptech could offer similar terms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found. The company failed on its own financing and operations.

market_need_then: Landlords have vacancy risk and want speed. Evidence of demand in 2017 beyond the YC description was not found. A Rental Beast mention comes only from CB Insights without a date.

branding.domain_note: Used rentrezi.com, not rezi.com, per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered funding and the collapse, not the brand. The name needed a prefix in its domain, and a branding search found no brand coverage.

pivots.to: Guaranteed rent and leasing of vacant apartments
pivots.why: One summary of a YC interview says the shift addressed landlord vacancy risk. Not verified against the interview itself.

outcome_analysis: Rezi raised a $30M Series A in 2018 and then financed its rent guarantees with roughly $200M of debt in 2022 and 2023. Credit lines ran dry in November 2023 and the company shut down in early 2024, with the founder citing unprofitable scaling and higher interest rates. Landlords and a staffing firm reported unpaid bills afterward.
notes: The directory status is Active but sources show a 2024 shutdown, so the directory is stale. Company site rentrezi.com could not be fetched (host not resolvable in this session). Seed of March 2017 with undisclosed amount appears only on CB Insights, and a September 2023 Series B plus a February 2023 second $100M loan (lender conflicting between sources) appear only in a search summary or aggregators, so they are not recorded as rounds. Total funding estimates of about $230M come from aggregators. Shutdown date given as 2024 because sources say early 2024.
